title: 1998 Paris–Granada–Dakar Rally
who: Won by Jean-Pierre Fontenay / Gilles Picard (Mitsubishi) and Stéphane Peterhansel (Yamaha)
summary: The 1998 edition of the Dakar Rally, in its African era: 19 stage towns and bivouacs through France, Spain, Morocco, Mauritania, Mali, Senegal. Winners — Cars: Jean-Pierre Fontenay / Gilles Picard (Mitsubishi); Bikes: Stéphane Peterhansel (Yamaha); Trucks: Karel Loprais / Radomír Stachura / Jan Cermak (Tatra 815).

sources.label: Motorsport.com: list of Dakar car winners

approximate: Stage towns and bivouacs from Wikipedia's stage table. The rally ran off-road between them, so the lines are straight from bivouac to bivouac.

stops.name: Paris
stops.text: The 20th Dakar starts from Paris again.

stops.name: Narbonne
stops.text: End of stage 1, with a 10 km special.

stops.name: Almeria
stops.text: Stage 3 to the port of Almería, then the crossing to Morocco.

stops.name: Ouarzazate
stops.text: Stage 5: 344 km timed over the Atlas.

stops.name: Smara
stops.text: Stage 6: 354 km timed into Western Sahara.

stops.name: El Mreiti
stops.text: Stage 8: 680 km timed into the empty north-east.

stops.name: Taoudenni
stops.text: Stage 9: 478 km to the salt mines of Taoudenni in northern Mali.

stops.name: Gao
stops.text: Stage 10 to Gao was cancelled; a rest day followed.

stops.name: Tidjikja
stops.text: Stage 13: 745 km timed, the longest special.

stops.name: Dakar
stops.text: The finish. Jean-Pierre Fontenay won the cars for Mitsubishi, and Stéphane Peterhansel the bikes on a Yamaha, his sixth, a record at the time.
